page: Microsoft Azure E96-24ds_v6 is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor. It features 24 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 12 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, running at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The processor includes a 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for tile and INT8 operations.

The server is equipped with 768.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high resource density of 32.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, it bundles 5669 GB of NVMe SSD capacity and is capable of utilizing Premium Storage. No GPU accelerators are included in this configuration.

In benchmark testing, the instance demonstrates strong memory performance, achieving an uncached read memory bandwidth of 190.74 GB/sec and an uncached write bandwidth of 120.18 GB/sec, both placing in the top 25%. Geekbench testing highlights strong single-core performance with a score of 2156.0, alongside strong results in image and text processing. Large language model inference using a small 135M model yields a strong text generation speed of 286.32 tokens/sec, while other computational and database benchmarks generally perform in the average tier.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio and substantial local NVMe storage, this server offers qualitative cost efficiency for workloads requiring massive memory footprints without needing a proportional scaling of compute cores. It is highly suited for large-scale in-memory databases, data analytics, enterprise applications, and memory-intensive processing tasks.
